readout_other: TMS-elicited motor evoked potential (MEP) amplitude from first dorsal interosseous muscle
direction_notes: Continuous theta-burst TUS reduced M1 excitability (MEP amplitude) at both superficial (~5 mm, grey matter) and deep (~16 mm, white matter) targets, persisting for at least 30 min; sham TUS did not alter excitability. Intermittent theta-burst TUS produced no significant change in MEP amplitude at either depth.
safety_notes: Simulations aimed to ensure the temperature increase inside the skull did not exceed 0.1 degC; measured simulated temperature rises were 0.074 +/- 0.016 degC (superficial) and 0.049 +/- 0.009 degC (deep).

exposures.label: Superficial and deep M1 stimulation (continuous and intermittent theta-burst TUS)

target.label: hand representation area of M1, targeted at superficial (~5 mm, grey matter) and deep (~16 mm, white matter) focal depths

device.model: four-element spherical ultrasound transducer (three annular rings and a central disc)

timing.protocol_description: Continuous theta-burst TUS: 0.2 s bursts at 10% duty cycle repeated at 5 Hz for a total duration of 80 s (400 bursts, 8 s of cumulative sonication). Intermittent theta-burst TUS: 2 s trains (each comprising 10 bursts of 0.2 s at 10% duty cycle) repeated every 10 s over 400 s (40 trains, 400 bursts total, 8 s of cumulative sonication). Each participant received superficial, deep and sham TUS (Experiment 1) or superficial and deep TUS (Experiment 2), with at least 1 week between sessions.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Seventeen healthy volunteers (average ${ \tt a g e } = 2 8 . 5 \pm 1 0 . 1$ years) took part in the experiment.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Participants took part in five TUS sessions, during which they consistently experienced similar auditory stimuli from both the transducer and the masking noise.
source_quotes.randomised: Each participant underwent superficial TUS, deep TUS and sham TUS procedures, administered in random order.
source_quotes.sham_type: The sham TUS procedure was conducted similarly to the active TUS procedures, with the transducer in contact with the scalp, but no ultrasound energy was delivered to the brain.
source_quotes.auditory_control: Throughout all three paradigms, Gaussian white noise generated by a computer was delivered to the participants to efectively mask any auditory signals from the transducer.

flags.reason: Superficial (~5 mm, grey matter) and deep (~16 mm, white matter) stimulation both target M1 at the same 500 kHz frequency and are combined into one exposure per the target x frequency rule; the two depths are described in the target label and protocol_description rather than as separate exposures.

The paper states a 0.2 s 'burst' duration with a 10% duty cycle repeated at a 5 Hz theta frequency; pulse_duration_ms=20 ms is derived from duty_cycle/PRF (10%/5Hz) per the burst rule, since no separate explicit pulse duration is given.

80 s is the total duration of the continuous theta-burst protocol and 2 s is the individual train duration in the intermittent protocol; both protocols report 8 s of cumulative active sonication, described in protocol_description.

The paper does not use the word 'blind' explicitly; single-blinding of participants to condition is inferred from the sham design (transducer on scalp, no ultrasound delivered) and the statement that study objectives were not revealed to participants.
